yuezhuornis:study:1.title: Jurassic flightless bird reveals early ecological diversity of avialans (Nature, 2026)

facts.statement: The fossil range of Yuezhuornis spans the Late Jurassic Kimmeridgian to Tithonian ages.
Yuezhuornis is an extinct basal avialan known from a partial skeleton and skull from the Late Jurassic Nanyuan Formation of China.
facts.quote: Yuezhuornis () is an extinct genus of basal avialan known from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian–Tithonian ages) Nanyuan Formation of China.The genus contains a single species, Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, known from a partial skeleton and skull.

facts.statement: Yuezhuornis had significantly shorter arms than its closest relatives, making it incapable of flight.
facts.quote: It has significantly shorter arms than its closest relatives—being proportionally more similar to many non-avialan theropods—implying it was incapable of flight.

facts.statement: Yuezhuornis is a close relative of Zhengheornis, which is known from the same locality.
facts.quote: It was a close relative of Zhengheornis, which is known from the same locality.

facts.statement: Xu Liming and colleagues formally described Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis as a new genus and species in 2026, establishing IVPP V34427 as the holotype.
facts.quote: In 2026, Xu Liming and colleagues described Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis as a new genus and species of early avialan dinosaur based on these fossil remains, establishing IVPP V34427 as the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: The holotype individual of Y. yangyuanensis is estimated to have weighed about 821 g, based on femur width.
facts.quote: The Y. yangyuanensis holotype individual has an estimated body weight of around 821 g, derived from a calculation using the width of the femur.

facts.statement: Histological analysis indicates the holotype was near skeletal maturity, representing a subadult or adult individual.
facts.quote: Histological analysis suggests it was close to skeletal maturity when it died, belonging to a subadult or adult individual.

facts.statement: The humerus of Yuezhuornis is shorter than the femur, a proportion otherwise known only from some anchiornithids and the flightless euornithean Patagopteryx.
facts.quote: Also unlike early avialans, the humerus is shorter than the femur. A longer femur is only seen in some anchiornithids and the flightless euornithean Patagopteryx.

facts.statement: Its foot lacks the arctometatarsalian condition, resembling early avialans rather than dromaeosaurids or troodontids.
facts.quote: Unlike dromaeosaurids and troodontids, but more like early avialans, the foot has a non-arctometatarsal condition.

facts.statement: The second pedal digit of Yuezhuornis ends in a hyperextensible toe, similar to that of troodontids and dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: The last non-ungual phalanx of the second pedal (foot) digit is similar in morphology to that of troodontids and dromaeosaurids, indicative of a hyperextensible toe.
